name: Chrome Mox
oracle_text:
Imprint — When this artifact enters, you may exile a nonartifact, nonland card from your hand.
{T}: Add one mana of any of the exiled card's colors.
blocked_sentences: {T}: Add one mana of any of the exiled card's colors.

needs.what: a fourth dynamic-colour family for mana abilities, alongside 'reflecting' and 'in_commander_identity' and 'chosen_color_of': an add_mana whose producible colours are the printed colours of the cards a selector matches -- here {"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"} -- narrowed at activation time in costs.mana_options_of so the solver plans against the real colours, and empty (the ability makes nothing) while nothing is imprinted
needs.why_existing_wont_do: A mana ability may hold only add_mana or one choose_mode of add_mana, and each of the three existing narrowings asks the wrong question. 'reflecting' resolves a pool and asks each object's own mana abilities what it could produce, so an imprinted Lightning Bolt -- a card with no mana abilities at all -- would offer nothing rather than {R}; 'in_commander_identity' asks the command zone; 'chosen_color_of: self' reads a colour the permanent chose, and Chrome Mox names no colour, it reads the colours off another card. The colours of an exiled card are not a value the mana language can reach at all: value_keys has mana_value_of and colors_of_mana_spent but no colours-of-an-object leaf, and an op that could compute one (choose_color) is forbidden inside a mana ability. Leaving the packet's five-colour choose_mode in place would be a Mox Opal that taps for any colour with nothing imprinted -- the unconditional any-colour approximation the reflecting capability exists to refuse.
